--- BEGIN SOURCE: transfer-review.md ---

# Night-bus transfer review: test the timetable at Harbor Junction first

The municipal transport committee reviewed the September transfers from the
last inbound train to the night bus at Harbor Junction. Staff observed
17 missed transfers in the four weeks they logged. In 14 of those cases,
the bus had already left when a train arriving within its published time
reached the platform. Logs for the other three show train delays. The review
covers Harbor Junction only. It did not test whether a schedule change would
improve transfers.

The committee's explicit first trial is to move the last night bus departure
at Harbor Junction five minutes later for two weeks, without changing
departures at other stations. Dispatchers will log completed transfers and
onward delays before the committee decides whether to retain the change.
Better signs were discussed, but the committee set them aside for this
trial. The public briefing should explain the specific mismatch and what the
temporary timetable test will measure.

--- END SOURCE: transfer-review.md ---

idea.title: Plain-language public briefing for Harbor Junction night riders: the five‑minute timetable test explained
idea.description: A short, clear public briefing that explains (1) the specific mismatch found at Harbor Junction (buses leaving before trains that arrived within the published time), (2) the committee’s temporary change — moving the last night‑bus departure at Harbor Junction five minutes later for two weeks only and not changing other stations — (3) exactly what will be measured (dispatchers will log completed transfers and onward delays), and (4) the trial’s limits (Harbor Junction only; signage was discussed but not changed; the review did not test whether a schedule change would improve transfers broadly). The piece should tell riders what to expect during the two weeks and where to look for official follow‑up.
idea.audience: Night commuters who use Harbor Junction, local commuter groups and resident stakeholders, and local news outlets covering transport updates.
idea.rationale: Riders directly affected need to know the concrete problem, the narrow scope of the test, and how success will be judged so they can plan trips and interpret results. The main uncertainty is whether a 5‑minute shift will be sufficient and whether two weeks at one station will produce decisive evidence; the briefing should make those limits explicit to avoid overclaiming.
idea.evidence: Staff observed 17 missed transfers in the four weeks they logged; in 14 cases the bus had already left when a train arriving within its published time reached the platform; logs for the other three show train delays. The committee's explicit first trial is to move the last night bus departure at Harbor Junction five minutes later for two weeks, without changing departures at other stations. Dispatchers will log completed transfers and onward delays before the committee decides whether to retain the change. Better signs were discussed, but the committee set them aside for this trial. The review covers Harbor Junction only and did not test whether a schedule change would improve transfers.
